$comment: Scoop manifest template. The release workflow substitutes 0.5.10,
https://yoink.cdn.jumpmind.cloud/yoink/0.5.10/yoink-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip and 5b2a09372553fd2b022c3449221efd59203be3d079138c42568401f635bf3f5f and commits the result to the bucket repository.
https://yoink.cdn.jumpmind.cloud/yoink/0.5.10/yoink-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip is on the public downloads CDN, never a GitHub release: this
repository is private, so a GitHub URL is a 404 for everyone who would
install from a public bucket. There is no `checkver`/`autoupdate` for the
same reason: the release workflow pushes the new manifest itself, and
the GitHub API it would poll is not open to the public either.
5b2a09372553fd2b022c3449221efd59203be3d079138c42568401f635bf3f5f is read from the .sha256 the release publishes beside the
archive, the same one the patched PowerShell installer verifies against,
so there is exactly one published hash per archive.
post_install: Write-Host 'yoink installed. Run `yoink doctor` to check it over.'
